chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu 'Amr al-Sarraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
Regarding the man in whom the stolen goods are found, he said: 'He is liable (for debt/compensation) if he does not bring witnesses to prove the seller of the stolen goods.'

key_terms.غَارِمٌ: Liable / debtor (one who owes compensation or debt)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a person found with stolen goods in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of *Bab al-Gharar* (Chapter of Uncertainty), this narration clarifies the burden of proof in commercial transactions involving stolen property, establishing that possession alone does not absolve the buyer of liability (*gharam*) without verified evidence of the seller. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on preventing ambiguity (*gharar*) and ensuring financial justice by requiring witnesses to authenticate the source of goods, thereby protecting the original owner's rights.
